title: DNA Size Selection and Purification Using Improved Homemade SPRI Beads Solution
author: Ramawatar

steps.title: Prepare 10 mL bead stock
steps.instruction: In a 50 mL tube combine 100 µL 10 mM Tris‑HCl (pH 8), 20 µL 1 mM EDTA (pH 8), 3.2 mL 1.6 M NaCl and 4.24 mL Milli‑Q water; vortex. Then add 2.2 mL 11 % PEG 8000 (50 % w/v), 200 µL 0.25 % Tween‑20 (10 % v/v), and 40 µL Sera‑Mag SpeedBeads® (0.4 % v/v). Vortex thoroughly. This 10 mL solution is the homemade SPRI bead stock.

steps.title: Vortex and transfer beads
steps.instruction: Vortex the Sera‑Mag SpeedBeads® Carboxyl Magnetic Beads (GE Healthcare) vigorously, pipette 40 µL into a 1.5 mL tube, place the tube on a magnetic rack and wait until the beads collect at the tube wall.

steps.title: First bead wash
steps.instruction: Remove the supernatant, add 1 mL Milli‑Q water to the beads, mix gently, spin briefly in a microcentrifuge, and return the tube to the magnet.

steps.title: Re‑mix and re‑magnetize
steps.instruction: While on the magnet, mix the bead suspension well, spin down again, and place back on the magnet.

steps.title: Allow beads to collect
steps.instruction: Wait until the beads have fully assembled at the back of the tube and the solution is clear.

steps.title: Repeat bead washes
steps.instruction: Perform the wash sequence described in steps 3‑5 three additional times (total of four washes).

steps.title: Add stock solution to washed beads
steps.instruction: After the final supernatant removal, take the tube off the magnet, add 40 µL of the freshly prepared bead stock (from step 1), mix well, spin down, and transfer the entire mixture into the remaining stock solution in the 50 mL tube. Mix thoroughly.

steps.title: Add PEG to stock
steps.instruction: Add the remaining 2.2 mL of 50 % PEG 8000 to the 50 mL stock tube, vortex vigorously (PEG is viscous; pipette carefully). The final PEG concentration is critical for clean‑up performance.

steps.title: Adjust DNA sample volume
steps.instruction: Place the DNA sample in a 1.5 mL tube at a convenient volume (typically 20–200 µL). If the sample is highly viscous or contains many contaminants, dilute and split into two tubes to ease handling.

steps.title: Add bead solution to DNA
steps.instruction: Determine the exact sample volume (V). Add 1 × V of the room‑temperature bead solution (or 0.9 × V if you wish to remove more small fragments, accepting a higher risk of reduced recovery). Mix by flicking the tube.

steps.title: Incubate on rotor
steps.instruction: Place the tube on a rotor (or mixer) and mix for 10 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Centrifuge and magnetize
steps.instruction: Spin the tube briefly in a microcentrifuge, then place it on the magnetic rack.

steps.title: Wait for bead binding
steps.instruction: Allow the beads to migrate to the tube wall until the solution becomes clear (1 min to >1 h depending on viscosity). If beads remain in a cloudy mass, add the same volume of buffer and bead solution (maintaining the original ratio), mix, and re‑magnetize.

steps.title: Discard supernatant
steps.instruction: Remove and discard the clear supernatant without disturbing the bead pellet.

steps.title: First 70 % ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Add 1–1.5 mL 70 % ethanol to the side opposite the bead pellet, wait 30 seconds, then remove and discard the ethanol.

steps.title: Second 70 % ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Without removing the tube from the magnet, repeat the ethanol wash (add 1–1.5 mL 70 % ethanol, wait 30 seconds, discard).

steps.title: Remove residual ethanol
steps.instruction: Take the tube off the magnet, spin briefly to collect any remaining ethanol, place back on the magnet, and pipette off the last drops.

steps.title: Air‑dry beads
steps.instruction: Allow the beads to air‑dry for no more than 30 seconds; over‑drying hampers elution.

steps.title: Elute DNA
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL (or the desired final volume) of pre‑heated (50 °C) 10 mM Tris‑HCl (or TE buffer) to the beads and mix.

steps.title: Re‑magnetize elution
steps.instruction: Spin the tube briefly, place it on the magnet, and wait until the beads re‑collect (1 min to several hours; typically 5–10 min).

steps.title: Collect eluate
steps.instruction: When the solution is clear, pipette the supernatant (the purified DNA) into a fresh tube and discard the beads.

steps.title: Quantify DNA
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration using a Qubit fluorometer. Expected recovery for high‑molecular‑weight DNA (>20 kb) is 60–90 %.

steps.title: Run agarose gel QC
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1 % TBE agarose gel, load 80 ng DNA per lane (normalize to 10 µL), and run alongside a 1 kb ladder and the indicated SPRI bead test lanes for size‑selection assessment.
